title: Sonny and the Golden Hour | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka sits completely still as the sun sets and watches the whole bush turn gold — every leaf, every trunk, every piece of bark lit from the side by the most beautiful light of the day. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The light was changing.

Sunny had been sitting for a while, just sitting, when she noticed it. The colour of everything was slowly shifting — from the ordinary white light of afternoon to something else. Something warmer. Something gold.

She didn't move.

The light crept across the clearing. It touched the tops of the gum trees first — a warm amber glow on the very top of each trunk — then spread downward, covering everything. The grass turned from green to gold. The grey trunks turned red-gold. The bark, usually pale and unremarkable, glowed with a deep copper colour.

She held out her paw.

Her fur was lit from the side — each individual hair catching the light, so that her ordinary golden-brown was now something deeper. Something richer. She looked at her paw as if she had never seen it before.

The shadows were long and soft.

Everything was in relief — every blade of grass, every wrinkle of bark, every leaf edge caught the light at its angle and gave it back as something luminous.

She thought: this happens every day, and I almost always miss it.

The gold deepened, slowly, and then the sun dropped behind the trees and the light became softer, more violet, and the gold slipped away.

She stayed for the violet too.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, golden hour. Goodnight, little one.
